A neighborhood school, on purpose

Minlee Korean School (MKS LLC) runs out of a home-based studio in Santa Clara — and that smallness is the point. Young children learn a language fastest when they feel safe, known, and excited to come back next week.

Our students are heritage learners hearing Korean at home, and beginners whose families simply love the language and culture. Both belong here, in one mixed group. Class is spoken mainly in Korean, with English support whenever a child needs it — so no one is ever lost, and every child leaves having actually spoken Korean out loud.

We’re a bilingual school in every sense: this site, our emails with parents, and our classroom all move between English and Korean. 한국어 문의도 언제든 환영합니다.

Alongside the language, children meet the culture it lives in: folktales and picture books, holiday traditions like Seollal and Chuseok, traditional games, and the everyday words of family life — the Korean of grandparents, food, and home.

What children learn

  • Hangul consonants and vowels — sounds first, then first syllables
  • Greetings and everyday phrases: hello, thank you, please, goodbye
  • Numbers, colors, family words, animals, and food
  • Korean children’s songs and rhymes, sung every week
  • Picture-book stories, including Korean folktales
  • Hands-on crafting every week, tied to the week’s words
  • Culture days: hanbok, holiday foods, and traditional games

Questions parents ask

My child doesn’t speak any Korean. Is that okay?

Yes — 유아1반 is a first-Korean class. We teach in Korean with English support, and children pick up the routine words quickly because they hear them the same way every week.

We speak Korean at home. Will it still help?

Heritage learners benefit too: they build Hangul reading foundations, learn school and story vocabulary beyond home Korean, and get to use the language with friends their own age.

Is the class taught in Korean or English?

Mainly Korean — that’s how children pick it up naturally at this age. The teacher uses English support for instructions and whenever a child needs it, and we’re happy to talk with parents in English or Korean.

What should my child bring?

Just themselves and a water bottle. Tuition covers all books, materials, and craft supplies — there is no separate materials fee.

How big is the class?

Maximum 5 students, so every child speaks and is heard each week. Seats are reserved in order of inquiry, so email early if you’re interested.

Where do we park for drop-off and pick-up?

Street parking is available on Cypress Ave, a short walk from Pruneridge Golf Club. We’ll confirm the easiest spot in our reply to your inquiry.

How do we enroll, and what is tuition?

Enrollment starts with an email inquiry — use the form below or write to minlee.hlee@gmail.com. We’ll reply with tuition details and the mid-January semester calendar, and your child’s seat is reserved once you confirm.
